title: Adaptive quota smoothing for cache-driven coalesced batches
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers are seeing quota spikes and unexpected rate-limit rejections when prefix/KV cache hits cause many requests to be coalesced into a single inference batch. Metering currently attributes token usage per raw request or per physical batch inconsistently across cache-hit/miss cases, which creates unfair quota consumption for tenants with bursty access patterns.

Goal: Introduce an adaptive quota-smoothing layer that (1) deduplicates zero-cost tokens from prefix cache hits across coalesced batches, (2) applies a short per-tenant smoothing window to prorate token attribution for near-simultaneous requests that are merged by the runtime, and (3) ensures rate-limiter accounting reflects the smoothed usage so quotas and throttles behave predictably.

This ticket covers design, billing/metering pipeline changes, runtime flags for opt-in rollout, metrics, and a staged deployment plan.
acceptance_criteria: Metering pipeline emits both raw_token_count and smoothed_token_count for every request group
Rate-limiter consult uses smoothed_token_count and prevents false positive throttles during small bursts with heavy cache-hits
Billing compute matches smoothed_token_count for invoice generation and quota deductions in the billing datastore
Automated tests verify no double-charging for a representative set of scenarios (pure cache-hit, mixed hit/miss, concurrent multi-tenant merges)
Dashboard shows new metrics (smoothed_tokens, batch_coalescence_rate, per-tenant smoothing_credit) and regression alerts are configured
implementation_plan: Design: define smoothing window (initially 200ms) and credit policy; doc linked below
Add metadata headers on inference requests to preserve original request_ids and tenant_id through batching layer
Metering pipeline: compute raw_batch_token_sum, per-request token contributions, and produce smoothed attribution using dedupe+prorate logic
Rate-limiter integration: query smoothed tokens instead of raw before enforcing per-tenant token limits; add fallback to raw tokens if smoothing service unavailable
Billing path: write smoothed_token_count to billing_topic; adapt invoice generator and quota reconciler to read smoothed counts
Add feature flag 'billing.smoothing.v1' to gate rollout per-tenant and enable canary groups
End-to-end tests + integration tests for multi-tenant coalesced batches
Observability: implement metrics and traces; add dashboard and alert rules
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): Unit tests, local integration, and synthetic load verifying no regressions
Stage 1 (canary): Enable feature flag for internal tenants + 3 low-volume customers for 48h; monitor smoothed_vs_raw token delta
Stage 2 (gradual): Expand to 25% of production tenants over 7 days; set automatic rollback if charge divergence > 2% or throttles increase
Stage 3 (full): Flip default for all hosted customers and remove opt-in after 4 weeks of stable metrics
Rollback: Immediately disable feature flag and backfill raw counts to billing if critical regression detected
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after post-mortem on ENG-26411 showed billing spikes for tenant 'SynthRetail' during cache warmups. Initial design doc attached.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz: Spike reproduction harness implemented; confirmed that coalesced batches where 80% of requests were prefix-cache hits still charged full aggregate tokens. Proposed smoothing window 200ms based on observed inter-arrival times.

2026-03-12 - Liang Chen (review): Suggested we use per-tenant smoothing credits to prevent abuse where clients intentionally send rapid parallel requests to game credits. Also recommended a 1-request threshold to avoid smoothing single-request batches.
2026-03-12 - Product (Riley Thompson): Customer-facing impact accepted as medium. PM requests a billing-safe rollout and clear communication to early canary customers.
2026-03-13 - Security (Priya Menon): Confirmed no PII will be stored by smoothing service; recommended scoping audit logs to tenant_id hashes. No full security review required for v1.

2026-03-13 - Marco Ruiz: Implementation in progress: added request_id header passthrough and initial metering changes in branch feature/ENG-28765. Draft PR up for internal review. Planning canary for 2026-03-18.
